title: Hire window sprint costing corridor
summary: Working spreadsheet to evaluate 12-week hire windows across three sourcing mixes (aggressive hire, mixed hire+contingent, conservative contingent-first) and their impact on monthly burn and runway under three token pricing scenarios.
assumptions: Average fully-burdened SWE cost: $26k/month (includes benefits & infra allocation)
Committed GPU pool cost is modeled separately and grows with gross token demand
Token consumption baseline taken from July-2026 p50 usage; downstream demand scales +/- 20% under scenarios
Hiring lead time: 6 weeks from offer to productive contribution (partial productivity ramp at week 4)
sensitivity_scenarios: Scenario A - Token deflation: token price -20% (downside revenue pressure). Runway shortens by ~0.8-1.2 months across months with high committed GPU spend.
Scenario B - Token stability: token price flat (base case). Current committed GPU bands assumed adequate; runway per table applies.
Scenario C - Token surge: token price +25% (revenue helps runway). Option to accelerate hiring or convert contractors earlier.

Sourcing mix sensitivity: shifting 4 FTE from hires -> contractors lowers near-term burn by ~32k/mo but increases hiring risk and reduces medium-term productivity (modeled as 6% throughput loss on product roadmap).
Burst GPU contingency: 10% unplanned burst increases committed GPU $k by +15% and reduces runway by ~0.6 months under base token price.
conclusions: Near-term: if token prices decline more than 15% we should pause non-critical opens and shift two hires to contractor conversions to preserve runway.
Medium-term: mixed hire+contingent preserves velocity without immediate headcount lock-in; recommended for Oct-Nov window.
Capitalize on potential token surge by front-loading two critical hires in Jan-Feb if price signal remains for >6 weeks.
Operational: maintain a 12% committed GPU buffer and a formal burst fund of $200k to avoid reactive hiring freezes.
